overview.summary:
This bundle fixes two known todo defects as independent, thin vertical slices. S01 restores edit-dialog due date persistence without widening the todo editing surface; S02 restores the documented low-priority default for quick-add creation without entering the edit/update route owned by S01.

Both stories are intentionally parallel and conflict-averse. The plan keeps write ownership disjoint so the fixes can land independently and merge cleanly.

sharedDecisions.title: Disjoint route ownership
sharedDecisions.description: S01 owns the todo edit/update route surface; S02 must avoid `src/app/routes/todos.py` and restore the default priority through a different persistence seam so the stories do not collide.

sharedDecisions.title: Per-bug regression files
sharedDecisions.description: Each story gets its own focused regression test file so parallel execution does not force both stories into the same test module.

sharedDecisions.title: Current HTMX and route contracts stay intact
sharedDecisions.description: Both fixes preserve the existing HTML-partial and ad-hoc route-validation architecture; no story introduces JSON responses, Pydantic wiring, or auth changes.

bindingConstraints.verbatim: Story 1: BUG-002 - due dates set in the edit dialog do not persist after save.
Keep each story isolated to its own files; they must merge without conflict.
Story 2: BUG-003 - quick-add todos have no default priority.
Keep each story isolated to its own files; they must merge without conflict.

stories.name: Persist edit-dialog due dates
stories.scope: Ensure a due date chosen in the edit dialog survives save-and-reopen by aligning the edit form's date value with the server persistence path, while keeping the fix limited to todo edit behavior and a dedicated BUG-002 regression file. Excludes priority-default behavior, due-date styling, and broader todo-creation changes.
stories.notes: Own the todo edit/update surface only; avoid model-level default changes and avoid shared test modules with S02.

stories.name: Default quick-add priority to low
stories.scope: Ensure todos created through the quick-add flow always persist with the documented low priority so reopening the edit dialog shows a populated selector, while keeping the fix off the todo edit/update route and in a dedicated BUG-003 regression file. Excludes due-date parsing, visual priority styling, and broader todo-edit behavior.
stories.notes: Restore the default through a non-route persistence seam so the story stays merge-safe with S01.

riskSummary.mitigation: Pin the accepted edit-dialog date format in a dedicated BUG-002 regression test and verify save-and-reopen behavior against the stored todo.

executionNotes: Execute S01 and S02 in parallel within W1. Preserve the shared decision on disjoint write ownership: S01 may own the edit/update route surface, while S02 must restore the quick-add default through a different file surface and its own regression file. Treat full-file `tests/test_todos.py` runs as bundle-level validation after both stories land; each story's execution gate should use only its dedicated bug regression plus targeted pre-existing route checks.
